scenes.title: The Glass Mark Triangulation Technique
scenes.sub: The standard operating procedure behind every Sentinel Report investigation.
scenes.vo: Every investigation we publish is tested three ways before anyone sees it. Here is the procedure.
scenes.delivery: Flat and procedural. You are naming a method, not selling one.
scenes.source_note: Title of the methodology document. docs/GLASSMARK.md.

scenes.question: How do you know when a story is ready?

scenes.label: THE PURPOSE
scenes.quote: Dead ends are documented as dead ends. Nothing is published until it is sourced.
scenes.source: Source: The Glass Mark Triangulation Technique, SOP, June 2026
scenes.vo: Expert consensus gets compared against the finding. Every angle gets pursued. Nothing goes out unsourced.
scenes.delivery: This is the thesis. Slower than everything around it.
scenes.source_note: GREEN — verbatim from the purpose statement in docs/GLASSMARK.md.

scenes.caption: expert perspectives, pulled and compared.
scenes.sub: The goal is not to confirm what we already think. It is to test it, pressure it, and find where it needs more documentation.
scenes.vo: Three lenses. Not to confirm the story. To try to break it.
scenes.delivery: Land on the number, then let the caption do the work.

scenes.title: The domain expert.
scenes.sub: What does the leading researcher in this field already document about exactly this?
scenes.vo: First lens. What does the field already know? That sets the baseline.
scenes.delivery: Brisk. These three are a sequence — keep them moving.

scenes.title: The dissenting view.
scenes.sub: What is the strongest credible counterargument? What innocent explanation fits the same evidence?
scenes.vo: Second lens. Steelman the other side before publishing, not after.

scenes.title: The adjacent field.
scenes.sub: A sociologist reading a surveillance contract sees what a lawyer does not.
scenes.vo: Third lens. A different discipline surfaces the questions the first one stopped noticing.
scenes.delivery: Land it. This is the end of the sequence.

scenes.question: What if the dissent is right?

scenes.label: THE TEST
scenes.quote: If we can't answer the dissent with documented evidence, we're not ready to publish.
scenes.source: Source: The Glass Mark Triangulation Technique, Lens 2 — The Dissenting View
scenes.vo: That is the whole test. Not whether we believe it. Whether we can answer the strongest objection with a document.
scenes.delivery: The most important line in the episode. Slow, and stop after it.

scenes.question: What happens to the stories that don't survive?

scenes.label: DEAD END
scenes.quote: A documented dead end is still honest journalism.
scenes.source: Source: The Glass Mark Triangulation Technique, Step 5 — Classify The Result
scenes.vo: If the experts explain it, we write down that they explained it, and we move on. That is a result too.
scenes.delivery: Warm here, not grim. This is the line people will repeat.

scenes.question: So what is the first story?
scenes.source_note: Host scene. Film yourself here. This is the hook into episode 01.

scenes.title: Every build carries a receipt.
scenes.sub: The method is enforced in code — a claim without a source does not render.
scenes.vo: Every render writes a manifest. The spec, every file it read, the video itself. Anyone can check.
scenes.delivery: Close it out. Let the hash finish typing before you stop.
